name: Jotham (Jerubbaal's (Gideon's) youngest son who survived Abimelech's massacre)
title: Gideon's youngest son and teller of fables
summary: Jotham was the youngest of Gideon's (Jerubbaal's) seventy sons and the only one to survive the massacre carried out by their half-brother Abimelech. He is best known for his fable about the trees seeking to choose a king, which he told from Mount Gerizim as a prophetic warning to the people of Shechem. His prophetic curse was fulfilled when Abimelech and the citizens of Shechem destroyed each other.

keyEvents.title: Abimelech's massacre of Gideon's sons
keyEvents.description: Abimelech, Gideon's son by a concubine from Shechem, killed his seventy brothers on one stone. Only the youngest, Jotham, survived by hiding.

keyEvents.title: Jotham's fable about the trees
keyEvents.description: From the top of Mount Gerizim, Jotham told a fable about the trees seeking to anoint a king over themselves, but only the thornbush accepted. The fable was a sharp critique of Abimelech's kingship and the treachery of Shechem's citizens.

keyEvents.title: Jotham's warning to Shechem
keyEvents.description: After the fable, Jotham directly challenged the people of Shechem, asking whether they had acted rightly toward the house of Jerubbaal, and declared that fire would come from Abimelech to consume the citizens of Shechem, and vice versa.

keyEvents.title: Jotham Flees to Beer
keyEvents.description: After delivering his prophetic speech, Jotham fled to Beer, where he settled in safety, away from the threat of his half-brother Abimelech.

keyEvents.title: The Fulfillment of Jotham's Curse
keyEvents.description: After three years, the citizens of Shechem turned against Abimelech, and in the ensuing conflict both the inhabitants of Shechem and Abimelech himself were killed, exactly as Jotham had prophesied.
